claims.quote: On average, Logic-LM achieves a significant performance boost of 39.2% over using LLM alone with standard prompting

says.measure: accuracy gain over standard prompting

claims.quote: Logic-LM also improves CoT by a large margin of 18.4% on average

says.measure: accuracy gain over chain-of-thought

claims.quote: GPT-4’s performance is notably less promising, with Exe_Rate scores of 79.9% and 32.6% respectively

says.measure: share of generated programs that run (GPT-4, AR-LSAT)

claims.quote: self-refinement is effective in fixing the in-executable symbolic formulations, increasing the Exe_Rate by 5.01 on average

says.measure: executable-rate gain from repair with solver errors (points)

claims.quote: We also introduce a self-refinement module, which utilizes the symbolic solver’s error messages to revise symbolic formalizations.
However, the accuracy tends to stagnate in subsequent rounds, even though the Exe_Rate continues to increase.
When used with GPT-4, LINC scores 26% higher than CoT on ProofWriter while performing comparatively on FOLIO.

says.measure: accuracy gain over chain-of-thought (GPT-4, ProofWriter)

claims.quote: the FOL expressions sometimes contain syntax errors: 38% for StarCoderPlus, 24% for GPT-3.5, and 13% for GPT-4

says.measure: generated logic programs with syntax errors (GPT-4)

claims.quote: SatLM outperforms program-aided LMs by 23% on a challenging subset of the GSM arithmetic reasoning dataset

says.measure: accuracy gain over program-aided LMs (GSM-Sys)

claims.quote: SatLM ’s selective accuracy is consistently better than ProgLM ’s, especially on GSM-Sys (77% vs 45%)

says.measure: selective accuracy when abstaining on UNSAT or ambiguous specs (GSM-Sys)

claims.quote: Unlike the executor used in ProgLM that can only detect errors in code execution, SAT solver can spot UNSAT and AMBIG in addition to ERROR .
Our current approach parses a problem into a SAT specification, runs the solver, and returns the answer in a one-round fashion.
with a relative accuracy gain of 6.3% on Math Word Problems (MWP), 3.4% on Planning, 5.5% on Multi-hop Question Answering (QA), and 21.4% on Relational Inference

says.measure: relative accuracy gain over chain-of-thought (relational inference)

claims.quote: the likely primary cause is the sparsity of Datalog in the pretraining data for Codex, as an overwhelming 29% of errors are syntax-related

says.measure: share of errors that are Datalog syntax errors (StrategyQA)

claims.quote: On TransCoder and MBPP where unit tests are available, Self-Debugging improves the baseline accuracy by up to 12 %

says.measure: accuracy gain over no debugging (with unit tests)

claims.quote: Self-Debugging instructs the model to execute the code, then generate a feedback message based on the code and its execution result.
drawing 10 samples up front and then 1 repair candidate each (up to 20 samples total) leads to a pass rate 1.05 ×

says.measure: pass rate over i.i.d. sampling at equal budget (GPT-4, APPS)

claims.quote: replacing GPT-4’s own explanations with those of a human programmer improves repair significantly, increasing the fraction of repaired programs which pass the tests by a factor of 1.58 ×

says.measure: repaired programs passing tests over model's own feedback (GPT-4)

claims.quote: current models are held back by their inability to reliably produce accurate and useful feedback on why the code is wrong

says.covers: feedback on why code is wrong

claims.quote: drawing 2 samples up front and then drawing 10 repair candidates each (up to 22 samples total) leads to a pass rate which is lower than the baseline pass@22 ( 0.97 ×

says.measure: pass rate over i.i.d. sampling at equal budget (GPT-4, APPS, 2 initial + 10 repairs)

claims.quote: grammar-constrained decoding (GCD) can be used to control the generation of LMs, guaranteeing that the output follows a given structure
We see a significant improvement when constraining the generation to only produce valid entities and relations.
we introduce a type-constrained decoding approach that leverages type systems to guide code generation
LLMs frequently generate code with typing errors, which are beyond the domain of syntax and generally hard to adequately constrain
We observe declines in LLMs’ reasoning abilities under format restrictions, with stricter constraints generally leading to greater performance degradation in reasoning tasks.
we found that 100% of GPT 3.5 Turbo JSON-mode responses placed the "answer" key before the "reason" key

says.measure: responses that put the answer key before the reasoning key (GPT-3.5, Last Letter)

claims.quote: Comparing NL-to-Format with unrestricted Natural Language responses, we observe nearly identical performance across most models
Constrained decoding can speed up the generation process by 50% compared to unconstrained decoding.

says.measure: generation speedup over unconstrained decoding

claims.quote: Constrained decoding consistently improves the performance of downstream tasks up to 4%, even for tasks with minimal structure like GSM8k.

says.measure: downstream accuracy gain over unconstrained decoding

claims.quote: evaluate six state-of-the-art constrained decoding frameworks, including Guidance , Outlines , Llamacpp , XGrammar , OpenAI , and Gemini .
showing up to 10% points accuracy improvement over baselines on challenging symbolic reasoning benchmarks GSM-symbolic and FOLIO

says.measure: accuracy gain over constrained and unconstrained decoding (GSM-Symbolic, FOLIO)

claims.quote: it is always possible to preserve the reasoning capabilities of the LLM while ensuring syntactic and semantic correctness in its outputs
We ran our tool on three mature engines and found 13 previously unknown query bugs

says.measure: previously unknown query bugs found in three engines

claims.quote: we present the first metamorphic-testing approach for detecting query bugs in Datalog engines
We implement our approach in DLSmith, which detected 16 previously unknown query bugs in four Datalog engines.

says.measure: previously unknown query bugs found in four engines

claims.quote: evaluated Deopt on four mature Datalog engines, namely Soufflé, CozoDB, µZ, and DDlog, and discovered a total of 30 bugs

says.measure: bugs found in four engines

claims.quote: The core idea behind the test oracle is to compare the results of an optimized program and a program without cross-rule optimization; any difference indicates a bug in the Datalog engine.
our incremental approach can produce 1.17 × \times (for DDlog) to 31.02 × \times (for Soufflé) as many valid test cases with non-empty results as the naive random method

says.measure: valid non-empty test cases over naive random generation (60 rules)
